text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- FINAME LENDS 18 PERCENT LESS IN 1997

The value of total loans by Brazil's National Development Bank for the purchase of machinery and equipment in the first five months of this year has shrunk 18.1 percent in comparison with the same period last year.
-- RE-ELECTION BILL IS SANCTIONED
The Brazilian Congress has ratified a bill allowing President Cardoso, as well as governors and mayors to run for a second consecutive term in office in the next elections.
-- COELBA MINIMUM PRICE SET AT 975 MLN REAIS
A 65.64-percent stake in Bahia state electricity distributor Coelba will go on sale July 31 at a base price of 975 million reais.
O ESTADO DE SAO PAULO
-- QUALIFIED BIDDERS FOR CELLULAR BAND B CONCESSIONS NAMED
The government has announced a list of 10 qualified bidders for cellular Band B telephone concessions.
-- INQUIRY SAYS MALUF MISAPPROPRIATED 1.2 BLN REAIS
An inquiry into a scandal involving state and municipal bonds concluded that former Sao Paulo mayor Paulo Maluf misappropriated 1.2 billion reais from the sale of bonds.
O GLOBO
-- CELLULAR PRICES FALL 52 PCT IN BRASILIA ON PRIVATIZATION
The privatization of Brazil's cellular Band B telephone services has led to a cut in price for buying a line in Brasilia of 52 percent.
-- COUNTRY SELLS $3 BLN IN BONDS ABROAD
The Brazilian government successfully sold abroad $3 billion worth of 30-year bonds.
-- THEFT OF IMPORTED LUXURY CARS IS ON THE RISE
The theft of imported luxury cars, which was practically unheard of three years ago, is on the rise in Rio de Janeiro.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
